As we wrap up our journey through My Grandmother’s Hands by Resmaa Menakem, let’s take a moment to really let the heart of this message sink in. This isn’t just about understanding trauma—it’s about transforming it, starting with ourselves, and rippling out to our families and communities. The wisdom here feels both timeless and incredibly urgent for the world we live in today.
So, what are the big takeaways? Well, first, healing starts with tuning in and honoring the signals your body sends. Even the smallest, most consistent practices can help your nervous system move toward a place of safety and ease.
And here’s the thing—healing doesn’t have to be lonely. When communities come together to witness and support one another, real, collective change becomes possible. Repairing relationships takes being present, honest, and sometimes, brave enough to make amends.
Justice and healing? They go hand in hand. Both call for steady, courageous action, day after day.
If you ever catch yourself bracing against the world, just remember—you’re not alone in this. The patterns you carry aren’t your fault, but you have the power to shift them. It happens one breath, one pause, one gentle act of care at a time. Healing can feel slow, maybe even frustrating, but it’s always within reach.
Every time you practice settling your body, or reach out to someone else, you’re adding to something bigger—a movement that honors the pain of the past, while building a future filled with justice, belonging, and hope.
So trust that your efforts really do matter, even when it’s hard to see progress. Every small act of healing is a gift—not just to yourself, but to everyone who comes after you.
